issue_context.title: Add telemetry for v0.26.0
issue_context.body:
To keep the transparency with our users, here are the added telemetries to our product. We need to add them to the docs, @meilisearch/docs-team.

- [ ] add telemetry for the CLI flags and options, see [this spec changes](https://github.com/meilisearch/specifications/pull/107).

⚠️ User data are still anonymized and you can easily disable the analytics by passing the `--no-analytics=true` flag when launching MeiliSearch.

More about the [MeiliSearch telemetry usage](https://docs.meilisearch.com/learn/what_is_meilisearch/telemetry.html#telemetry).
comments: Description updated according to this comment https://github.com/meilisearch/specifications/pull/106#issuecomment-1016876691

review_comments: We should maybe also check that it is different from `localhost:7700` as this is equivalent even if it is not the default value.

I can but I think the idea was just to see if the field has been used, not really how people use it :thinking: 
What do you think @gmourier?
Absolutely, it's all about whether this option is used.

Also, what I don't like here is that we serialize all of the Argument struct and pick the field that we don't want to for privacy reasons instead of doing it the other, safer, way: picking the struct fields that we care about and are safe. Doing it the other way can work with privacy if we forgot about modifying this block of code: we would lose information instead of getting too much from the user i.e. privacy argument.

Or maybe I am wrong and the `#[serde(skip)]` thing is enough.
A great example is the `snapshot_dir` field that leaks information about the user filesystem that we don't want to know about, and we forgot to serde skip it and to change the value to a boolean.

Yes, basically we need to choose if we want to maintain a big chunk of code importing every field one by one or if we want to import everything by default and *try to remember* to erase the thing containing user data.
I thought doing it like that was what @MarinPostma proposed Monday but I can change it.
I am for skipping field as @Kerollmops said
